concern_rules.reason: Promotes cellular turnover and stimulates collagen synthesis to diminish fine lines.
concern_rules.citation: Kafi R, et al. Improvement of naturally aged skin with vitamin A (retinol). Arch Dermatol. 2007.

concern_rules.reason: Prevents follicular plugging by accelerating epidermal desquamation.
concern_rules.citation: Leyden J, et al. Why Topical Retinoids Are Mainstay of Therapy for Acne. Dermatol Ther. 2017.

concern_rules.reason: May induce retinoid dermatitis, escalating erythema and transient barrier irritation.
concern_rules.citation: Mukherjee S, et al. Retinoids in the treatment of skin aging. Clin Interv Aging. 2006.

concern_rules.reason: Cleaves stratum corneum desmosomes to smooth uneven roughness.
concern_rules.citation: Tang SC, Yang JH. Dual Effects of Alpha-Hydroxy Acids on the Skin. Molecules. 2018.

concern_rules.reason: Low pH acids can irritate sensitive capillaries and worsen erythema.
concern_rules.citation: Babilas P, et al. Cosmetic and dermatologic use of alpha hydroxy acids. JDDG. 2012.

concern_rules.reason: Lipophilic salicylic acid penetrates sebum inside pores to dissolve keratin plugs.
concern_rules.citation: Arif T. Salicylic acid as a peeling agent: a comprehensive review. Clin Cosmet Investig Dermatol. 2015.

concern_rules.reason: Regulates surface sebum accumulation through lipophilic exfoliation.
concern_rules.citation: Kligman AM. Salicylic acid: an alternative to alpha-hydroxy acids. J Geriatr Dermatol. 1997.

concern_rules.reason: Inhibits tyrosinase activity to impede melanogenesis and fade hyperpigmentation.
concern_rules.citation: Al-Niaimi F, Chiang NYZ. Topical Vitamin C and the Skin: Mechanisms of Action and Clinical Applications. JCAD. 2017.

concern_rules.reason: Suppresses melanosome transfer from melanocytes to surrounding keratinocytes.
concern_rules.citation: Hakozaki T, et al. The effect of niacinamide on reducing cutaneous pigmentation. Br J Dermatol. 2002.

concern_rules.reason: Fortifies ceramide synthesis and reduces cutaneous vascular inflammation.
concern_rules.citation: Draelos ZD, et al. Niacinamide-containing facial moisturizer improves skin barrier. Cutis. 2005.

concern_rules.reason: Humectant capable of binding up to 1,000 times its molecular weight in water.
concern_rules.citation: Papakonstantinou E, et al. Hyaluronic acid: A key molecule in skin aging. Dermatoendocrinol. 2012.

concern_rules.reason: Replenishes physiological lipid bilayer to prevent transepidermal water loss (TEWL).
concern_rules.citation: Meckfessel MH, Brandt S. The structure, function, and importance of ceramides in skin and their use as therapeutic agents in skin-care products. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2014.

concern_rules.reason: Common contact allergen that frequently triggers flushing, reactive erythema, or dermatitis.
concern_rules.citation: Johansen JD. Fragrance contact allergy: a worldwide issue. Contact Dermatitis. 2003.

concern_rules.reason: Volatile alcohol strips essential epidermal lipids, worsening dehydration and barrier dryness.
concern_rules.citation: Lachenmeier DW. Safety evaluation of topical applications of ethanol on the skin and inside the oral cavity. J Occup Med Toxicol. 2008.

concern_rules.reason: Releases free oxygen radicals bactericidal against Cutibacterium acnes.
concern_rules.citation: Sagransky M, et al. Benzoyl peroxide: a review of its current use in the treatment of acne vulgaris. Expert Opin Pharmacother. 2009.

concern_rules.reason: Potent oxidative mechanism often induces scaling, dryness, and contact erythema.
concern_rules.citation: Tanghetti EA, et al. Optimizing the use of benzoyl peroxide in acne vulgaris. J Drugs Dermatol. 2009.

conflict_rules.warning: Combining Retinoids with Alpha Hydroxy Acids (AHAs) drastically elevates irritation, flaking, and skin barrier compromise.
conflict_rules.recommendation: Alternate usage between morning and evening, or cycle on separate nights.

conflict_rules.warning: Using Retinoids simultaneously with Beta Hydroxy Acids (Salicylic Acid) can lead to excessive dryness and epidermal stinging.
conflict_rules.recommendation: Use BHA in the morning or on non-retinoid days.

conflict_rules.warning: Benzoyl Peroxide oxidizes and may deactivate classic retinol, while multiplying redness and peeling.
conflict_rules.recommendation: Apply Benzoyl Peroxide in the AM and Retinoid in the PM.

conflict_rules.warning: Layering Pure L-Ascorbic Acid with exfoliating AHAs can over-acidify the skin mantle, inducing stinging or redness.
conflict_rules.recommendation: Reserve Vitamin C for morning antioxidant defense and AHA for evening exfoliation.
